name: Outdoor Recreation & Safety

objectives.text: Name items that belong in a basic outdoor safety kit, such as water, a hat, sunscreen, and a whistle
Explain why outdoor helpers stay with a buddy and a trusted adult and what to do if separated from the group
Identify common outdoor hazards in the local area, such as poison ivy, ticks, stinging insects, and venomous snakes
Describe the safety rules for a common outdoor activity, such as hiking, fishing, or camping
Explain basic water safety rules, including wearing a properly fitted life jacket on and near the water
Demonstrate the safe handling, passing, and storage of a pocketknife and other basic camp tools
Describe the seven Leave No Trace principles and give an outdoor example of each
Demonstrate how to read a trail map and use a compass to plan and follow a safe route outdoors
Tie and use basic outdoor knots, such as the square knot, bowline, and two half hitches, for camp and shelter tasks
Demonstrate safe campfire site selection, building, tending, and complete extinguishing
Use a GPS unit or mapping app together with a topographic map to locate and record waypoints
Explain how to prepare for and respond to weather hazards such as lightning, flash floods, and high winds during an outdoor outing
Demonstrate basic first aid for common outdoor injuries, such as cuts, blisters, sprains, and insect stings
Recognize the signs of heat exhaustion, heat stroke, dehydration, and hypothermia and describe the proper field response to each
Demonstrate hunter education firearm and archery safety practices, including safe carries, zones of fire, and tree stand safety
Explain the state hunting, fishing, and boating license and safety requirements and how they protect participants and wildlife
Select and inspect personal protective and safety gear, such as life jackets, blaze orange, helmets, and harnesses, for proper fit and condition
Apply Leave No Trace principles while planning a multi-day outdoor recreation trip
Describe the economic impact of outdoor recreation such as hunting, fishing, and agritourism on local and state economies
Assess options for improving the sustainability of a local outdoor recreation site based on resource impact and likelihood of user acceptance
Recommend changes that make an outdoor recreation activity more sustainable while keeping it accessible and equitable for all participants
Evaluate management techniques, such as trail design, access control, and habitat improvement, for improving outdoor recreation opportunities on public or private land
Manage the planning and risk assessment for a group outdoor excursion, including gear, route, weather contingencies, and emergency procedures
Develop a safety and compliance checklist to evaluate an outdoor recreation enterprise or SAE, such as a guiding or hunting lease operation, against required regulations

changes: Kept all six original competencies, rewording a few for precision. Added a buddy system objective at grade 2, local hazards, water safety, knife safety, Leave No Trace basics, knots, campfire safety, GPS navigation, first aid, and heat and cold illness for the younger grades. For high school, added hunter education safety, licensing and safety requirements, protective gear inspection, the economics of outdoor recreation, recreation sustainability and management assessments, and an SAE compliance checklist. Each high school objective is anchored to the matching AFNR codes, and stewardship theology, policy ethics, and careers are left to the sibling sub-topics.
